narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and your job type. The short nine-month duration you asked for was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward approval. Most approved applicants request almost twice as long (19 months on average), so your brief repayment period counted as a clear positive signal.

Unfortunately, two other important factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction and ultimately outweighed that advantage. Your checking account is currently in negative balance (less than 0 DM). Only about 13% of approved applicants are in this situation, so the model viewed it as a meaningful risk indicator. Your job as a manager or self-employed professional also worked against you. While this might seem surprising, the model has learned that, in this dataset, people in highly skilled or self-employed roles are statistically more likely to default than those in standard skilled occupations.

Taken together, the negative signals from your account status and job type were strong enough to overcome the benefit of the short loan term, resulting in denial.

You should focus on building a positive checking-account balance and, if possible, reapply with a slightly longer loan period that better matches what successful applicants typically request. These two changes would likely improve your chances on a future application. (248 words)
